pr_title: Update new session RMap expiration in changeSessionId
pr_comments: Since the plan is to deprecate `RedissonSessionRepository`, this fix isn’t needed.

issue_context.title: RedissonSession map doesn’t have expiration after changeSessionId is called
issue_context.body: We noticed a large number of keys in our Redis server had no TTL set and traced it back to the `RMap` that backs the session.
comments: I think I could deprecate my own Spring Session Manager in favour of Spring's implementation. I wrote this Manager when Redisson didn't have spring-data-redis implementation. Since Spring's implementation based on it Redisson Spring Session Manager could be dropped. What do you think?

> > I think I could deprecate my own Spring Session Manager in favour of Spring's implementation
> 
> this makes sense to me, and it looks like it will be a quick change for us to switch to Spring’s session repository.

After a bit more investigation, there’s one blocker for this: Spring’s implementation unconditionally [uses `rename` in `changeSessionID`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-session/blob/e6e02de210db41a86f283ece0d9f0b78ed27e864/spring-session-data-redis/src/main/java/org/springframework/session/data/redis/RedisIndexedSessionRepository.java#L837), which causes `CROSSSLOT` errors (the same as #1897).

It looks like other implementations of `RedisConnection` have special handling for `rename`: if the new key hashes to a different slot, it uses `dump`, `restore` and `del` to emulate the command. I can open a PR, if this sounds reasonable.

> I can open a PR, if this sounds reasonable.

Yeah, I would consider it.

review_comments:
We’re almost duplicating `updateExpiration()` here, with two key differences:
- we’re copying the existing TTls, rather than setting to the maximum
- we’re using a batch, so it will be faster

However, I think we’d be OK to just call `updateExpiration()`.
